messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Significant improvement in muscle spasm and pain occurred by day 3 or 4 of treatment.
1
With Amrix extended-release capsules, the drug is first detectable in the blood about 1.5 hours after a dose.
Peak levels occur at 7 to 8 hours.
One daily dose provides day-long coverage.

How long does cyclobenzaprine stay in your system?
:
Cyclobenzaprine stays in your system for about 3 to 7 days after your last dose.
It has a half-life of around 18 hours for the immediate-release tablets.
A drug takes 4 to 5 half-lives to clear from the body.
1
The once-daily forms last longer.
The half-life is about 32 hours for Amrix extended-release capsules and about 36 hours for Tonmya sublingual tablets.
These can take a week or more to fully clear.
Cyclobenzaprine also stays in the body longer in older adults.
It stays in the body longer in people with liver problems.
In people with liver problems, blood levels run higher.
1,2,3
Does cyclobenzaprine show up on a drug test?
:
Cyclobenzaprine does not usually show up on a drug test.
Cyclobenzaprine is not a controlled substance.
Triples: [["Cyclobenzaprine", "has effect", "significant improvement in muscle spasm and pain"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "detectable in blood after", "1.5 hours"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "peak levels occur at", "7 to 8 hours"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has administration instruction", "one daily dose provides day-long coverage"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has duration in system", "3 to 7 days"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has half life", "18 hours for immediate-release tablets"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has clearance time", "4 to 5 half-lives"], ["Amrix extended-release capsules", "has half life", "32 hours"], ["Tonmya sublingual tablets", "has half life", "36 hours"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has duration in system", "week or more for extended-release forms"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has increased duration in", "older adults"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has increased duration in", "people with liver problems"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has increased blood levels in", "people with liver problems"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "does not show up on", "drug test"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "is not", "controlled substance"]]
Relations: ["detectable in blood after", "does not show up on", "has administration instruction", "has clearance time", "has duration in system", "has effect", "has half life", "has increased blood levels in", "has increased duration in", "is not", "peak levels occur at"]
Answer:

completion:
detectable in blood after: The subject drug becomes detectable in the blood at the time specified by the object entity.  
does not show up on: The subject drug is not detected by the test or method specified by the object entity.  
has administration instruction: The subject drug is administered according to the instruction specified by the object entity.  
has clearance time: The subject drug takes the time specified by the object entity to be cleared from the body.  
has duration in system: The subject drug remains in the body for the duration specified by the object entity.  
has effect: The subject drug produces the therapeutic or physiological effect specified by the object entity.  
has half life: The subject drug has the half-life duration specified by the object entity.  
has increased blood levels in: The subject drug remains at higher concentrations in the population or group specified by the object entity.  
has increased duration in: The subject drug remains in the body for a longer duration in the population or group specified by the object entity.  
is not: The subject entity is not classified or categorized as the object entity.  
peak levels occur at: The subject drug reaches its maximum concentration in the blood at the time specified by the object entity.
